Serilog.//: Sinks must be named here. Serilog.Settings.Configuration finds them by scanning the ENTRY assembly's dependencies, which under dotnet test is the test host, not this app - so a sink discovered fine at runtime silently vanishes in tests.

//Https: Port is the site's own HTTPS binding, used to build the redirect target. Leaving it unset does NOT disable the redirect - the middleware then tries to discover a port from the server's bindings and, failing that, passes the request through unredirected with nothing but a warning. Set it. Development is exempt from the redirect entirely, so this has no effect there.

Atlassian.//: Source and Target identify tenant roles. Shipped tenant settings are synthetic placeholders.
Atlassian.//BaseUrl: The site a person visits. Every link and every URL written into an issue - including the attachment URLs embedded in a copied description - is built from this, so it must stay the real site.

Source.//ExcludedIssueTypes: Xray test-management types. Excluded in the JQL rather than at the mapping stage - a type that is never read cannot be mis-mapped.

Target.//ProjectName: Display name shown beside the project key to clarify the destination.
Target.//SourceUrlFieldName: Holds the source issue's URL so a reader can open the original. Also the duplicate check, with the summary: both must match exactly.

Mapping.//: Decisions, not discoveries. The six Xray types are excluded at the query instead. A missing entry surfaces as a blocker in the plan rather than a guess.
Mapping.//IssueTypes: Source type name -> target type name, for the cases an exact name match gets wrong. Empty on purpose: the rule is now 'the five shared types match by name, everything else falls back'. Adding an entry here overrides both.
Mapping.//Constants: Target field NAME -> literal value, for fields the target requires that the source has no equivalent of. Populate from what phase0-surface.ps1 reports as required-with-no-default.
Mapping.//FallbackIssueType: Anything the target has no same-named type for becomes this. Epic, Story, Bug, Task and Sub-task match by name and are untouched; Improvement, New Feature, Production Issue and Config Change all land here. Empty would mean fail instead of fall back.

//OAuth: The 3LO app's identity. Register it with an ACCOUNT-LEVEL grant so one sign-in reaches both tenants. Empty is a legitimate state, but without it nobody can sign in and nothing can reach either tenant - there is no API-token path any more. NEVER put ClientSecret here: this file is not gitignored and IS copied into the publish output. Use 'dotnet user-secrets set OAuth:ClientSecret <value>' in development, or the OAuth__ClientSecret environment variable in production. CallbackUrl must match the app's registered callback exactly, trailing slash included.
